messages:
Eli (AcmeCorp): Hey team — started seeing a spike in p95 latency for our production calls. About 15-25% of requests that should go to eu-west are being served from us-west. This started ~2026-03-15 09:00 UTC. Example req id: req_0a9f. Any idea why our private VPC traffic would be picked up by the wrong region?

Nina (support): Sorry about that — we'll dig in. Are you on Redwood Private/VPC? Do you have a dedicated peering or are you going through a shared hub?

Eli (AcmeCorp): Private VPC with a peered hub (customer-peering-1) to Redwood. We use an on-prem SD-WAN -> hub -> cloud path. Our app is pinned to eu-west. We see X-Request-Id same as the req id, but the egress SNAT IP in our flow logs is 18.205.33.42 (which is US-ish).

Maya (infra): Can you paste a sample request wire/logs header (no PII) and a tcpdump/snippet of the upstream TCP flow? Also confirming: our smart-routing primarily uses the observed source IP to map geo affinity unless a VPC-level override exists.

Eli (AcmeCorp): Minimal headers:
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-Request-Id: req_0a9f
```
From our egress NAT capture (on-prem):
```
10.1.12.34 -> 18.205.33.42:443  (SNAT performed at hub edge)
```
We also see the peering BGP session to Redwood advertised from our hub via a transit, but the public SNAT IP is owned by the transit provider.

Arjun (networking): Thanks — that SNAT IP is the likely root cause. Our region selection routing table maps incoming source IP geolocation to a regional affinity. If the SNAT public IP geolocates to the US, the request will route to us-west. Do you control the NAT IP range at the egress or is it provider-owned?

Eli (AcmeCorp): Provider-owned. We don't control the SNAT. We assumed the private peering would preserve source IP but the hub does SNAT to provider public addresses for outbound.

Nina (support): That matches what we're seeing in our logs for req_0a9f — the observed peer IP on our edge was 18.205.33.42 and the routing decision selected us-west. I pulled a few request traces:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z - req_0a9f - peer=18.205.33.42 - routed(us-west) - model=redwood-v1
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z - req_0a9f+1 - peer=18.205.33.42 - routed(us-west)
```
So it's deterministic based on egress IP.

Maya (infra): Quick options:
- If you can provide us the NATed public IP ranges (or ASN) used by your transit/hub, we can add them to a customer exception list to preserve eu-west affinity.
- If that's not possible, we can adjust routing for your account to prefer eu-west based on VPC id/peering connection rather than source geolocation. That requires a short config rollout (can be done safely with canary).

Eli (AcmeCorp): We can get the list of NAT IPs from the transit provider, but it's likely dynamic. How invasive is the VPC-id-based routing change?

Arjun (networking): VPC-id routing is straightforward on our side: we attach a per-customer affinity rule so all traffic from that VPC/peering goes to the pinned region regardless of source IP. We use that for some enterprise customers who have large NAT pools. It does require a config entry on the control plane and a rolling update to routing tables — low risk but needs approval for production rollout window.

Nina (support): Short-term workaround: can you set the hub to add the original client IP into the `X-Forwarded-For` or `Forwarded` header (and not replace it) so our edge can detect `X-Forwarded-For: <your-public-nat>, <original-client-ip>`? We currently prefer direct source IP mapping but will read X-Forwarded-For for Private peering if present and signed/trusted.

Eli (AcmeCorp): Hub doesn't currently preserve X-Forwarded-For for TLS passthrough; it's terminating and re-initiating TLS, so it is adding the provider SNAT. I'll ask them to preserve and forward the original IP chain (or at least add `X-Redwood-Client-IP`).

Maya (infra): Two notes: 1) We only honor forwarded headers from peering connections that are in our trusted peering list — include the peering id in your message to us. 2) If they can't preserve original IPs, provide the up-to-date set of SNAT public prefixes and we will add them to an exception mapping to keep you in eu-west.

Eli (AcmeCorp): Peering id: pep-9832. I'll request the NAT ranges — transit said they'll provide a /20 and may rotate a few addresses. ETA ~2 hours. Also, is there any billing/SLAs impact if traffic routes to us-west temporarily? We're seeing higher latency but still within 5xx-free thresholds.

Nina (support): No billing change. Performance impact is only increased latency. We'll mark this P2 since it's customer-facing perf regression. I'll attach the trace logs and open an internal config change ticket if you give the NAT list or want the VPC-id override.

deploy-bot: Routing-config-change created: change-3712 (route-affinity: pep-9832 -> eu-west override). CI/CD run queued.

Arjun (networking): I'll standby for the NAT IP list. If you can't get a stable list, we can temporarily apply change-3712 for you and run a phased canary to ensure nothing else regresses. Once they provide stable prefixes we can make a permanent mapping and remove the override.

Eli (AcmeCorp): Received NAT list from transit: 18.205.33.0/24, 3.8.12.0/24. Sending now.

Nina (support): Got it. Applying exception: adding 18.205.33.0/24 and 3.8.12.0/24 to customer pep-9832 geolocation-exception list and activating canary 2% -> 25% -> 100%. Will post updates.

Maya (infra): Canary started: 2% of flows for pep-9832 now forced to eu-west. Monitoring latency and error rates.

(5m)
Nina (support): Canary 25% -> no error/no regression, latency p95 trending down for canary flows.

(10m)
Nina (support): Canary 100% complete. All pep-9832 traffic now routed to eu-west. Historical traces for req_0a9f show later attempts served from eu-west.

Eli (AcmeCorp): Confirmed — p95 back to normal. Thank you. What's the long-term recommendation?

Maya (infra): Long-term: two options:
1) Ask transit/hub to preserve client source IP (or append a trusted forwarded header). Then no exceptions needed.
2) If transit uses provider-owned SNAT you can't control, continue to provide public NAT prefixes and we'll maintain a mapping (recommended for enterprise customers).
Either way, we'll document the exception and add a note to your account.

Eli (AcmeCorp): We'll pursue preserving X-Forwarded-For with the hub and keep the prefix list as fallback. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Nina (support): Glad we could help. I'll keep the ticket open until you confirm the hub header change. Closing once you sign off. :thumbsup:
